details: Measured 27 Oct, change wt/owner-notes: a fixer repaired the Python 3.9 import in lib/relay_queue.py but not its copies under plugins/core/lib and plugins/front/lib; the next gate (about 15 minutes) went red only on "lib copies identical ... run bin/sync-lib-copies", and a third fix round was needed. The copies are kept by hand through bin/sync-lib-copies, which nothing runs for the agent; the gate is the first place that notices. Principle 2 (waste built into the setup) and principle 10 (the obvious way is the right way).
Also: the worker's quiet check
Also: plugins/core/lib, plugins/front/lib
failing_case: Edit lib/relay_queue.py in a worktree, commit, run the quick check the worker loops on: it passes; the gate then fails on 'lib copies identical'.
pass_cases: After an edit to a file under lib/ that has plugin copies, the copies are brought up to date without the agent having to know bin/sync-lib-copies (the quiet check or the commit step does it, or the copies stop being copies).
The gate's 'lib copies identical' step stays as the safety net.
A test shows the stale copy is caught or refreshed before the gate, and fails with that step disabled.
reason: tests/test_precheck.py:53 stale-copy test passes on head; on base 5fa711ed314e the tests error (relay_precheck absent). Gate keeps the lib copies step.
findings.summary: A fix to lib/ leaves the plugins' copies stale

details: CONFIRMED by a scratch test on the cycle harness. fixUnit sends `ask(it.fix, ...)` verbatim; quiet(it) is used for
the change kind's build, fix and red-gate fixer and for the checker only. The design (A.2) and the cycle comment say
"the worker, fixer and checker prompts all carry it ... so a brief or an item that names only a test line cannot
leave it out"; a fix unit (a re-fix after a check) is exactly the item that names only its own text. The new test
covers the change kind only, so it passes with this gap. Size: 10 min.
evidence: scratch test (Cycle harness, kind="fix"):
fix: x | NO precheck | Fix it.
check: x | precheck | Check: `review.json`. Fixes: ...
cycle.js:229  const f = await ask(it.fix, agentOpts('fixer', HANDBACK, 'Fix', `fix: ${it.name}`))
failing_case: Relay mode, items = [{kind: "fix", name: "x", wt, check: "pytest -q", fix: "Fix it.", fixes, findings, item: "i"}].
The prompt of "fix: x" is "Fix it." with no `relay precheck -C <wt> && pytest -q`; only "check: x" carries it.
It should carry the same quiet check the change-kind fixer gets.
fix_hint: ask(`${it.fix} Check: ${quiet(it)}.`, ...) in fixUnit, and extend the cycle test with a fix-kind unit.
pass_cases: 1. Relay mode, fix-kind unit: the "fix: x" prompt contains "relay precheck -C <wt> && pytest -q".
2. Relay mode, fix-kind unit: the "check: x" prompt still contains it (works today).
3. Project mode (relay false), fix-kind unit: no prompt contains "precheck"; the "fix: x" prompt contains the front's fix text.
4. Relay mode, change-kind unit: build, fix red gate 1, fix and check prompts keep it (test_every_quiet_check_starts_with_the_precheck).
reason: tests/test_cycle_workflow.py fix-unit test passes; unchanged since the earlier check.
findings.summary: a fix-kind unit's fixer gets the front's fix text alone: no relay precheck in its quiet check

details: CONFIRMED in a scratch repo. run() takes realpath(worktree) as the root: bin/types-lint is looked up there (missing:
skipped), plugins/*/lib is globbed there (none: ok), and `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD` run from a subdirectory

lists paths relative to it, so no plugins/

/lib/relay_*.py matches and the step is ok. An error answered as
success: the command a person runs by hand from where they stand says green. The cycle passes -C <wt> (the root), so
the cycle path is safe; a worker or the owner in a subfolder is not. Size: 10 min.
evidence: $ relay precheck -C r2/tests   ->  skip types and lint / ok python 3.9 / ok lib copies identical / precheck: green, rc=0
$ relay precheck -C r2         ->  FAIL plugins/core/lib/relay_q.py differs from lib/relay_q.py ... / precheck: RED
failing_case: A repo with lib/relay_q.py "X = 1" and plugins/core/lib/relay_q.py "X = 0", committed. `relay precheck -C <repo>/tests`
(or `relay precheck` run in <repo>/tests) prints "skip types and lint", "ok python 3.9", "ok lib copies identical",
"precheck: green", exit 0. It should check the repository the folder is in and fail naming plugins/core/lib/relay_q.py.
fix_hint: Resolve the root with `git -C <worktree> rev-parse --show-toplevel` in run() (fail when it fails) and use it for all three steps.
pass_cases: 1. -C <repo>/tests on the repo above: exit 1, output names plugins/core/lib/relay_q.py and bin/sync-lib-copies.
2. -C <repo> on the same repo: exit 1, same lines (works today).
3. -C <repo>/tests with identical copies: exit 0, "ok lib copies identical".
4. -C a folder that is not in a git repository: exit 1 with "cannot read HEAD" (works today).
reason: Met in the earlier check (tests/test_precheck.py); passes on head.
findings.summary: relay precheck from a subdirectory (or -C <subdir>) is green while a lib copy is stale

details: CONFIRMED by reading: lib/relay_ci.py main() keeps library tests, types and lint, hook tests, lib copies in that order
and runs every step after a red one. The brief says "build exactly A, unless the code proves it wrong; then say
where"; A has three items and its decided list leaves out only B, C, D and the contention measure. The worker's
report says item 3 was left out as "not in the brief's decided list, touches the inert probe comparison", which is a
risk named in the design, not a proof that it is wrong. The front or the owner may move it to a queue item;
otherwise it is part of this change. Size: 30 min (order, early stop with the inert probe stopped, tests).
evidence: lib/relay_ci.py:455-460 step order: library tests, types and lint, hook tests, lib copies identical, ...
design-speed.md A.3: "bin/ci runs the seconds-long steps first, and on the first red step reports at once"
reports/precheck.md: "Not built: bin/ci fail-fast step order (design A item 3 ...)"
failing_case: A branch whose only fault is a stale plugin copy reaches relay gate (the precheck skipped or run on an older head).
Today: library tests (263-662 s) and hook tests (149-354 s) run first; "lib copies identical FAILED" shows after
about 7-17 minutes. Design A.3: bin/ci runs the seconds-long steps first and reports the first red one at once; a
full green gate still runs every step.
fix_hint: Move types and lint and lib copies identical first in main(); when one is red, stop the probe and end RED; or, by the
front's word, a queue item for A.3 and this finding recorded as moved there.
pass_cases: 1. A tree with a stale plugin copy: bin/ci --quick prints "lib copies identical FAILED" before "library tests" starts, and ends RED.
2. A tree with a ruff error: types and lint FAILED is printed first, gate RED, within seconds.
3. A green tree: every step runs (library tests, types and lint, hook tests, lib copies, grader tests, plugin validate, inert), ends green.
4. Under relay gate the inert step's comparison still matches outer and probe runs (the probe runs the same order).
reason: Met in the earlier check (5ad0e9d step order); tests/test_ci_python.py passes on head.
findings.summary: design A item 3 not built: the gate still runs 7.5 minutes before a red seconds-long step shows

details: PLAUSIBLE as to how often (most relay change work goes through the cycle), CONFIRMED as to the text: only cycle.js
prepends the precheck; the delegate SKILL.md template line "Check: <command>  # the quiet check to loop on",
plugins/delegate/agents/worker.md ("loops on the project's quiet check"), kit_packet_rules.md ("Loop on the quiet
check (gate.check ...)") and rules/quality-gate.md are unchanged, and relay's .claude/kit.toml names no gate.check.
The worker listed these as "Callers not updated". The brief named both routes; the change built one. A text change
in a skill or agent needs the wave's paid run. Size: 15 min.
evidence: git grep -n -i "quiet check" -- roles rules plugins/delegate plugins/core:
plugins/core/lib/kit_packet_rules.md:7: Loop on the quiet check (`gate.check` ...)
plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md:61: Check: <command>  # the quiet check to loop on
cat .claude/kit.toml -> [delegate] max_parallel = 6 (no [gate] check)
failing_case: The front writes a brief by the delegate skill template ("Check: ~/.local/bin/pytest tests -q -k 'queue'") and
starts a worker on it without the cycle, in the relay repository. The worker loops on that line only; a stale
plugin copy or a mypy error reaches the gate, as in the five red gates of 27 Oct. The brief's decision: "Whatever
command the worker brief and the cycle script name as the quiet check must include it, so every future brief gets
it without being told."
fix_hint: Cheapest single source: relay's .claude/kit.toml [gate] check naming `relay precheck`, which the worker packet already
loops on; or one line in the delegate skill's Check template for projects with .relay/.
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the place a worker brief takes its quiet check from (the delegate skill's Check line, or the project's gate.check that kit_packet_rules.md points the worker at) names `relay precheck -C <worktree>` first for the relay repository.
2. Artifact: the cycle keeps prepending it (cycle.js quiet()).
3. A project without .relay/ is not told to run relay precheck.
reason: Met in the earlier check (SKILL.md text, tests/test_cycle_workflow.py); passes on head.
findings.summary: a worker started from a brief outside the cycle still loops on the front's test line alone

details: CONFIRMED by reading: check_python39 repeats test_lib_modules_import and test_hooks_survive_an_empty_event line for
line, its own old_python included. Correct today, fragile. Size: 10 min.
evidence: diff of lib/relay_precheck.py:45-70 and tests/test_py39_hooks.py:12-35: same globs, same -c code, same stderr filter.
failing_case: Someone tightens tests/test_py39_hooks.py (the gate's test), for example to fail on ImportError in a hook. The
precheck's check_python39 keeps the old rule: precheck green, gate red, the very drift this change removes for lib copies.
pass_cases: 1. tests/test_py39_hooks.py and relay precheck judge a module by one function (the test calls relay_precheck.check_python39, or precheck runs the test).
2. A plugin lib module with `match` fails both (works today in both).
3. A plain module passes both (works today).
reason: Met in the earlier check; tests pass.
findings.summary: the 3.9 step is a second copy of tests/test_py39_hooks.py; the two can drift

details: CONFIRMED with a scratch hook. The filter was written for annotation TypeErrors and syntax; the failure of 27 Oct
(owner-notes a6b8fb3c) was an ImportError of TypeGuard, caught only because it was in a lib module, not a hook. The
precheck copied the same filter (F5), so a fix there covers both when they share one function. Size: 15 min.
evidence: python3 -c "relay_precheck.check_python39('<scratch>')" -> []
/usr/bin/python3 <scratch>/plugins/core/hooks/new-hook.py <<< '{}' -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomllib', rc=1
failing_case: plugins/core/hooks/new-hook.py with "import tomllib" at the top. /usr/bin/python3 (3.9.6) on it exits 1 with
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomllib'. test_hooks_survive_an_empty_event passes (it looks only for
"TypeError" and "SyntaxError"), and relay_precheck.check_python39 returns []. On a Mac whose hook PATH python3 is
3.9 the hook dies on every event. It should fail naming the hook.
fix_hint: Also fail on "ImportError" / "ModuleNotFoundError" in stderr, or import each hook as a module under 3.9 without running main.
pass_cases: 1. A hook with "import tomllib" at module level: the 3.9 test fails naming the hook.
2. A hook with "from typing import TypeGuard" at module level: fails.
3. Every hook in the repo today on "{}": passes (none raises at import).
4. A hook that exits non-zero on "{}" for a reason after its imports (a KeyError in main): judged by the rule the fix picks, stated in the test.
reason: Met in the earlier check; tests/test_py39_hooks.py passes.
findings.summary: a hook that fails to import on Python 3.9 (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError) passes the gate's 3.9 test and the precheck

details: CONFIRMED by shell precedence; the checks the front writes today are single commands, so correct today. Size: 5 min.
evidence: cycle.js:114 const quiet = (it) => RELAY ? `relay precheck -C ${it.wt} && ${it.check}` : it.check
failing_case: Unit check "pytest tests/a.py; pytest tests/b.py". Quiet check becomes
"relay precheck -C wt && pytest tests/a.py; pytest tests/b.py": with the precheck red, tests/b.py still runs and its
exit 0 is the command's status. It should exit non-zero.
pass_cases: 1. check "a; b", precheck red: the prompt's command is "relay precheck -C <wt> && { a; b; }" (or parenthesised), so it exits non-zero.
2. check "pytest -q": the prompt still holds "relay precheck -C <wt> && pytest -q" or its grouped form, and the relay-command parser of the cycle test still reads "relay precheck -C <wt>".
reason: Met in the earlier check; tests pass.
findings.summary: relay precheck -C wt && <check> lets a check with ; or || hide a red precheck's exit code

details: CONFIRMED by reading: only check_types catches TimeoutExpired; _git and the 3.9 runs do not; the comment on
STEP_TIMEOUT calls it "the design's bound for the whole precheck" but it bounds each call. Size: 15 min.
evidence: lib/relay_precheck.py:20 STEP_TIMEOUT = 60  # ... the design's bound for the whole precheck
lib/relay_precheck.py:59,65 subprocess.run(..., timeout=STEP_TIMEOUT) with no except
failing_case: A hook that hangs on "{}" under /usr/bin/python3: subprocess.run raises TimeoutExpired after 60 s, uncaught in
check_python39; relay precheck ends with a Python traceback and no later step runs. With ~30 modules and hooks each
bounded at 60 s the whole precheck has no bound. Design A settings: "precheck time budget default 30 s, bound 60 s;
a test fails when the precheck on the repo takes longer"; no such test exists.
fix_hint: One deadline for the run, TimeoutExpired caught per step as a RED line, and one timing test on the repo.
pass_cases: 1. A step whose subprocess times out: the step is RED with "took longer than N s", the later steps still run, exit 1.
2. A test runs the precheck on the repository and fails when it takes longer than the bound.
3. The live repo: green in under 30 s (measured 6.6 s today).
reason: Met in the earlier check; tests pass.
findings.summary: the design's precheck time bound (30 s budget, 60 s bound, a test on the repo) is a 60 s limit per subprocess, and a timeout there is a traceback

details: CONFIRMED by reading and by the /nonexistent and scratch runs ("ok python 3.9" with no module). Not wrong in its exit
code, unclear in its words. Size: 5 min.
evidence: relay precheck -C /nonexistent -> "ok   python 3.9"

fix_hint: Return a "skipped: no plugin modules here" line when the globs or the HEAD listing find none.
pass_cases: 1. A repo with no plugins/*/lib files: "skip python 3.9 (...)" and "skip lib copies identical (...)", exit 0.
2. The relay repo: "ok" for each step (works today).
3. A stale copy: RED (works today).
reason: Met in the earlier check; tests pass.
findings.summary: a step that found nothing to check prints ok: in another .relay project precheck says green having checked nothing
